interaction_type.value: strain/stress concentration at (Nb,Mo,W)C–austenite interfaces leading to microcrack nucleation and microvoid formation

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: The (Nb,Mo,W)C particles located at the austenite grain boundaries act as hard second-phase particles leading to strain/stress concentration at their interfaces due to deformation discrepancy with the austenite matrix, tending to serve as preferential nucleation sites for microcracks; the concentration could be partially alleviated through debonding of intragranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and subsequent formation of microvoids.

slip_behavior.value: Predominant dislocation planar glide producing planar slip bands and Taylor lattice; slip bands refine with strain and then microbands with ill-defined and distinct boundaries form. For HR68, microbands were already observed at engineering strain 0.2.

interface_notes.value: For HR68 the submicron-sized particle was identified as a Nb-rich, Fe/Mn/Al-depleted (Nb,Mo,W)C particle with FCC structure (SAED [110] zone axis); no particle outline for C, Mo or W in EDS maps.

other_conditions.value: Uniaxial tensile tests on an MTS tensile machine; extensometer used; interrupted at engineering strains of 10%, 20%, 40% before fracture.
